# File Organization
1. Create a new R Markdown file called `practice_02.Rmd` in your `comm_106` folder. 
2. Download the Titanic Survival Dataset -- it should be called `titanic.csv`, and put it in your `comm_106` folder. 

# Package Installation 
In practice_01, we used a lot of functions that come with base R -- like adding numerics to each other and printing characters. However, there's a lot more stuff that we can do with R, using *packages* that have already been created by other people. 
When you get a new phone, you can send a picture of your cat to ten of your friends by individually messaging them. Or, you can download Instagram and post the picture of your cat on there. Packages for R are the same concept. If you haven't downloaded Instagram on your phone, your phone doesn't know how to post a picture of your cat on there. 

## tidyverse 
We will be using the tidyverse package. 

### Installing Packages

Run install.packages("tidyverse") in a R chunk.

````{.markdown filename="my-analysis.qmd"}
```{{r}}
install.packages("tidyverse")
```
````
You only have to do this once. (If you turn off your phone, you don't have to redownload Instagram everytime)

### Loading Packages
In order to actually use the package, you need to load it with every session with the **library()** function
````{.markdown filename="my-analysis.qmd"}
```{{r}}
library(tidyverse)
# Note that there are no quotation marks around tidyverse
```
````

# Loading the dataset
We'll be using data on the passengers of the Titanic. 
## The Dataset 
Here's what the first rows of the dataset look like. Each row is a passenger, and we have information on each passenger's Name, Sex, Age, and so on. 

## Load the dataframe in with the read_csv() function 
We assign the dataframe as a value to a variable called `df` 
(This is just common practice in data science, since it's easy to remember -- df stands for dataframe. You can name it whatever you want). 




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
df <- read_csv("titanic.csv")
```
:::
